variations.name: Fermentation & synbio platform chemicals from sugars
variations.description: Engineered microbes ferment plant sugars directly into high-volume chemical building blocks (diols, diacids, monomers, solvents) that drop into existing supply chains at up to ~90% lower greenhouse-gas emissions than petrochemical routes.

companies.name: Geno (Genomatica)
companies.what: Licenses single-step fermentation to make bio-BDO (1,4-butanediol) and other intermediates from plant sugars for spandex, packaging and personal care.
companies.signal: World's largest Geno bio-BDO plant started in Eddyville, Iowa; Hyosung TNC investing ~$1B in Vietnam plants; ~150 kt/yr licensed capacity in operation/construction.

companies.name: Cathay Biotech (Cathay Industrial Biotech)
companies.what: Large-scale fermentation of bio-based long-chain diacids (DDDA) and PA56 bio-nylon (TERRYL/ECOPENT) from sugar feedstocks.
companies.signal: STAR-listed; ~$456M trailing-12-mo revenue (Sep 2025); 2024 net profit ~487M yuan; partnering CATL on polyamide composites.

companies.name: Visolis
companies.what: Ferments biomass to mevalonic acid, then chemically converts it to bio-isoprene (rubber monomer), SAF and specialty solvents.
companies.signal: Zeon partnership toward a commercial bio-isoprene plant (announced 2025); >$5M U.S. DoD/DBIMP funding for bio-based solvents.

companies.name: ZymoChem
companies.what: Carbon-efficient fermentation platform that avoids CO2 loss to make bio-based monomers (e.g., adipic acid, biodegradable superabsorbents).
companies.signal: $21M Series A led by Breakout Ventures with Lululemon and Toyota Ventures.

companies.name: Corbion
companies.what: World-scale fermentation of lactic acid and lactide, the monomer feedstock for PLA and a range of bio-chemicals.
companies.signal: Leading global lactic-acid producer; took full control of the former TotalEnergies Corbion PLA business (2024).

variations.name: Chemo-enzymatic & cell-free biomanufacturing
variations.description: Uses immobilized enzymes and/or metal catalysis (not whole living cells) to convert sugars and feedstocks into chemicals and ingredients, enabling higher yields, continuous operation and fewer purification steps than classical fermentation.

companies.name: Solugen
companies.what: "Bioforge" platform pairs enzymes with metal catalysis to make organic acids (glucaric, gluconic) from dextrose for water treatment, ag and cleaning.
companies.signal: $213.6M DOE conditional loan guarantee; Bioforge Marshall (MN), ~120 kt/yr across 3 lines, targeting startup ~2025.

companies.name: Debut Biotech
companies.what: Cell-free (immobilized-enzyme) biomanufacturing of high-value cosmetic actives and ingredients from low-value feedstocks.
companies.signal: ~$88M total raised incl. Series B led by L'Oréal BOLD; partners L'Oréal, DSM, DIC; ~80 employees.

companies.name: EnginZyme
companies.what: Cell-free biomanufacturing using engineered enzymes on solid supports to run metabolic pathways outside living cells.
companies.signal: Swedish cell-free platform company; current 2026 status not independently re-confirmed in this research.

variations.white_space: Cell-free and chemo-enzymatic routes are hard at commodity scale because of enzyme cost, cofactor regeneration and stability; the credible opening is high-value specialty/cosmetic actives, or pairing enzymes with cheap metal catalysis as Solugen does to reach larger commodity volumes.

variations.name: Waste-gas fermentation (CO/CO2 to ethanol, acetate, protein)
variations.description: Anaerobic acetogen and methanotroph microbes ferment industrial off-gases, syngas, captured CO2+H2 or methane into ethanol, acetic acid/acetate and single-cell protein, recycling carbon that would otherwise be emitted.

companies.name: LanzaTech
companies.what: Licenses gas-fermentation to convert steel-mill/industrial off-gas and MSW-derived syngas into ethanol and platform chemicals.
companies.signal: NASDAQ:LNZA; ~$9.3M Q3'25 revenue and going-concern warning (~$19.6M cash, Sep 2025); multiple licensed commercial plants in China; €40M EU Innovation Fund grant (Norway, 2025).

companies.name: Again
companies.what: Gas fermentation of CO2+H2 with ancient acetogens to make acetic acid/acetate and ammonium-sulphate fertilizer.
companies.signal: ~$43M raised; first full-scale plant TXS-1 with Helen (Finland), 10-yr offtake up to 50 kt/yr acetic acid.

companies.name: Circe Bioscience
companies.what: Aerobic gas fermentation of point-source CO2 into triglycerides (fats/oils) and other products (Wyss Institute tech).
companies.signal: DOE-backed pilot — billed as world's most advanced aerobic gas-fermentation facility — opened late 2024; removes ~3 kg CO2 per kg product.

companies.name: Calysta
companies.what: Methane (natural/bio-gas) fermentation to single-cell protein (FeedKind) for aquaculture/animal feed, a protein-for-chemicals analogue.
companies.signal: Calysseo JV commercial plant in Chongqing, China operating; second plant planned.

variations.name: CO2 electrolysis to CO, syngas, formate/formic acid, ethylene
variations.description: Electrochemical cells use renewable electricity to reduce CO2 (with water) directly into carbon monoxide, syngas, formic acid/formate, ethylene, methanol or ethanol — the C1/C2 building blocks for fuels and chemicals — at near-ambient conditions.

companies.name: Twelve
companies.what: CO2 electrolysis (CO/O2 membrane reactor) plus downstream synthesis to make CO, syngas and E-Jet sustainable aviation fuel.
companies.signal: $645M funding (TPG-led, incl. $200M Series C); AirPlant One in Moses Lake, WA commissioning ~2025; $6M DOE grant.

companies.name: OCOchem
companies.what: CO2 electrolyzer producing formic acid/formate ("e-formic") as a hydrogen/energy carrier and chemical feedstock.
companies.signal: Completed what it calls the world's largest CO2 electrolyzer for formate (commercial-grade 1.5 m2 gas-diffusion electrodes).

companies.name: Dioxycle
companies.what: Low-cost electrolyzers converting CO2 into ethylene, CO and ethanol for the chemicals industry.
companies.signal: Lab unit converts ~10 kg CO2/day; first large industrial prototype targeted 2026; backed by Breakthrough Energy Ventures and Lombard Odier.

companies.name: CERT Systems
companies.what: CO2 electrolysis (clean electricity + water) to ethylene, ethanol and methane.
companies.signal: >$6M non-dilutive follow-on funding; AGC partnership for CO2-to-ethylene; Breakthrough Energy Innovator Fellow.

companies.name: Avantium (Volta Technology)
companies.what: Electrochemistry converting CO2 into formic, oxalic and glycolic acids and derivatives.
companies.signal: €3.5M EU grant (paid over 4 years from Jan 2025) for CO2 conversion; pilot stage.

companies.name: Oxylus Energy
companies.what: Direct low-temperature/low-pressure CO2-to-green-methanol electrolyzer (Yale-developed catalyst).
companies.signal: $4.5M seed co-led by Toyota Ventures and Azolla Ventures (Sep 2024).

companies.name: Sunfire
companies.what: High-temperature solid-oxide co-electrolysis (CO2+H2O) producing syngas for downstream e-fuels and chemicals.
companies.signal: German electrolyzer maker; SOEC/co-electrolysis deployed in Power-to-X projects; large alkaline+SOEC order book.

variations.name: Thermocatalytic CO2 hydrogenation & e-methanol plants
variations.description: Captured (often biogenic) CO2 is hydrogenated with green hydrogen over thermal catalysts to make e-methanol and e-fuels — drop-in feedstocks and low-carbon marine fuel — with the first commercial-scale plants now operating.

companies.name: Carbon Recycling International (CRI)
companies.what: Licenses Emissions-to-Liquids methanol-synthesis technology; pioneered the George Olah plant in Iceland and several Chinese plants.
companies.signal: Technology into one of the world's largest e-methanol plants (Tianying, ~170 kt/yr first phase); supplied Jiangsu Sailboat and Shunli CO2-to-methanol plants.

companies.name: European Energy
companies.what: Develops and co-owns e-methanol production; Kassø (Denmark) is the world's first large-scale commercial e-methanol facility.
companies.signal: Kassø inaugurated May 2025, up to 42 kt/yr; offtakers Maersk, LEGO, Novo Nordisk; first ISCC-EU RFNBO-certified e-methanol.

companies.name: Liquid Wind
companies.what: Develops standardized/modular e-methanol facilities and sells projects to investors/operators.
companies.signal: Four Swedish + two Finnish projects (~100 kt/yr each); €3.6M Swedish grant (2025); took over the suspended FlagshipONE project.

companies.name: HIF Global
companies.what: Produces e-methanol and e-fuels from CO2+green hydrogen; operates the Haru Oni demonstration plant in Chile.
companies.signal: Haru Oni producing since 2022; advancing large-scale e-fuels projects in Chile, US (Matagorda) and Australia.

companies.name: Topsoe
companies.what: Licenses methanol-synthesis catalysts and process technology underpinning many e-methanol and Power-to-X projects.
companies.signal: Technology provider to numerous global e-methanol/e-fuels developments.

variations.name: CO2- and methane-derived polymers (PHB from methane; CO2-polyols & polycarbonates)
variations.description: Methanotroph microbes turn methane into PHB/PHA bioplastics, while catalysts copolymerize waste CO2 into polyols and polycarbonates — embedding captured carbon directly into durable plastics, foams and elastomers.

companies.name: Newlight Technologies
companies.what: Methanotroph fermentation of (bio)methane + CO2 into PHB "AirCarbon" for foodware (Restore) and fashion (Covalent) goods.
companies.signal: Commercial-scale production facility in California; 15-yr methane-capture deal with CNX Resources; Carbon Trust carbon-negative certified.

companies.name: Mango Materials
companies.what: Methane (biogas/landfill) fermentation into PHA biopolymer for decentralized manufacturing at waste sites.
companies.signal: "Launch Facility" with 5,000 L fermentation; BioMADE-funded scale-up project (through Jun 2026); Allbirds and Stella McCartney prototypes.

companies.name: Econic Technologies
companies.what: Catalysts that copolymerize CO2 into polycarbonate-ether (PCE) polyols (Carnol) for polyurethanes.
companies.signal: Partner Changhua Chemical opened the world's first commercial-scale PCE-polyol plant (~80 kt in 2026, scaling toward >1M t); ~30% lower carbon footprint.

companies.name: Covestro
companies.what: cardyon CO2-based polyols (up to ~20% CO2) for flexible PU foams, elastomers and the first CO2-based thermoplastic polyurethane.
companies.signal: Commercial since 2016 at Dormagen, Germany; expanding CO2-technology applications.

companies.name: Asahi Kasei
companies.what: Licenses a phosgene-free polycarbonate process that incorporates CO2 as a raw material.
companies.signal: Non-phosgene CO2-based polycarbonate process widely licensed globally.

variations.name: Bio-based polymers & monomers (PLA, PHA, PEF, bio-PE, furanics)
variations.description: Polymers and monomers made from plant feedstocks — PLA, PHA, PEF, bio-polyethylene and furanics — that replace fossil plastics in packaging, fiber and durables, some compostable and some drop-in chemically identical resins.

companies.name: NatureWorks
companies.what: Ingeo PLA from sugar (lactic acid to lactide to PLA) for packaging, fiber, 3D printing and compostable serviceware.
companies.signal: Opened second fully-integrated PLA plant in Thailand (~75 kt/yr) in 2026; ~$350M Krungthai Bank financing.

companies.name: Braskem
companies.what: "I'm green" bio-polyethylene (and bio-EVA/bio-PP) from Brazilian sugarcane ethanol — drop-in renewable plastics.
companies.signal: World's largest bio-PE producer; expanding bio-based portfolio (showcased at K 2025).

companies.name: Avantium
companies.what: YXY technology converting plant sugars to FDCA, then PEF — a 100% bio-based, recyclable barrier polyester.
companies.signal: FDCA Flagship Plant in Delfzijl (5 kt/yr, ~€175M capex) commissioning; commercial sales expected Q1 2026; licensed tech to Origin Materials.

companies.name: Futerro
companies.what: Integrated lactic-acid and PLA producer/licensor (Belgium), developing a European PLA biorefinery.
companies.signal: PLA technology provider and producer positioning as a market leader in bioplastics.

companies.name: RWDC Industries
companies.what: Solon PHA from plant oils — biodegradable in soil, water and marine for single-use, packaging and coatings.
companies.signal: Trinseo partnership (Nov 2025) to advance PHA dispersion barrier coatings; TUV Austria biodegradation certifications.

companies.name: Kaneka
companies.what: Kaneka Biodegradable Polymer Green Planet (PHBH), a marine-degradable PHA from plant oils.
companies.signal: Commercial PHBH production in Japan with capacity expansion underway.

companies.name: Danimer Scientific
companies.what: Nodax PHA biopolymer (from plant oils) plus PLA-based resins for compostable packaging.
companies.signal: Filed Chapter 11 in March 2025 after ~$380M 2020 SPAC raise; wound down; operating assets and 480+ patents sold to Teknor Apex for $19M (June 2025).

companies.name: Origin Materials
companies.what: Originally CMF/furanics from biomass (Origin 1, Sarnia); now an asset-light furanics strategy after pivoting to PET caps & closures.
companies.signal: Shelved Geismar furanics plant (~$12.3M impairment); runs Origin 1 "on demand"; furanics commercialization paused while caps business ramps.

variations.name: Lignin & wood-derived chemicals and materials
variations.description: Biorefineries fractionate wood and black liquor into lignin and sugars, valorizing lignin into binders, phenol and carbon-black replacements, thermoplastics, vanillin and battery anodes while sugars become glycols and chemicals.

companies.name: Borregaard
companies.what: Operates one of the world's most advanced biorefineries, making lignosulfonates, bio-vanillin, specialty cellulose and fine chemicals from wood.
companies.signal: Long-profitable global lignin leader; multi-billion NOK revenue from biorefinery products.

companies.name: Stora Enso
companies.what: Lineo kraft lignin (phenol/binder/carbon-black replacement) and Lignode lignin-based battery anode material.
companies.signal: ~50 kt/yr lignin capacity — world's largest kraft-lignin producer; bio-based carbon pilot opened.

companies.name: UPM
companies.what: Leuna biorefinery turning hardwood into renewable glycols (bio-MEG/MPG) and lignin-based functional fillers replacing carbon black/silica.
companies.signal: Started industrial hydrothermal wood breakdown early 2025; 220 kt/yr capacity; first commercial products, with more in 1H 2026.

companies.name: Lignin Industries (RenCom)
companies.what: Renol lignin-based thermoplastic that blends into PE, PP and ABS at 15-30% to displace fossil plastic.
companies.signal: €3.9M raise (May 2025); distribution partnership with UK compounder Hellyar Plastics.

companies.name: Bloom Biorenewables
companies.what: Aldehyde-Assisted Fractionation converting lignin, cellulose and hemicellulose into chemicals and materials (DPX, lignin, cellulose) to replace petroleum.
companies.signal: CHF 13M (~$15M) Series A (Apr 2025) with Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Lombard Odier, Amcor and Btomorrow.

variations.name: Green surfactants, solvents & specialty ingredients (incl. on-site electrochemical H2O2)
variations.description: Fermentation-made biosurfactants (rhamnolipids, sophorolipids) and bio-based solvents replace petro/palm surfactants, while on-site electrochemical generators make hydrogen peroxide from air, water and electricity, cutting transport, storage and emissions.

companies.name: Evonik
companies.what: World's first industrial-scale rhamnolipid biosurfactant plant (fermentation from corn) for cleaning and personal care.
companies.signal: Triple-digit-€M plant in Slovenská Ľupča, Slovakia inaugurated May 2024; supplies Unilever cleaning products.

companies.name: Holiferm
companies.what: Yeast fermentation of sophorolipid biosurfactants using a separation-led continuous process.
companies.signal: >1,000 t/yr capacity, building 3,000 t/yr (15,000 t/yr planned); $23.1M Series B; BASF partnership.

companies.name: Sironix Renewables
companies.what: Eosix sugar/oil-derived surfactants that are sulfate- and 1,4-dioxane-free with strong cold/hard-water performance.
companies.signal: $3.5M round (Mar 2025, Arosa/Oval Park) plus ~$7M grants; scaling manufacturing; ~52% lower GHG vs petro.

companies.name: Locus Ingredients (Locus Performance Ingredients)
companies.what: Fermentation-produced sophorolipid biosurfactants (Ferma/Amphi lines) for home, industrial and personal care.
companies.signal: TSCA and EU REACH registrations; USDA 100% biobased; distributed by Dow as EcoSense.

companies.name: HPNow
companies.what: On-site electrochemical hydrogen-peroxide generators (HPGen) producing H2O2 from water, air and electricity for water treatment and oxidation.
companies.signal: DTU SurfCat spin-out; key patents granted; commercial deployments via water-treatment partners.

variations.name: Electrified synthesis beyond CO2 & catalyst-discovery platforms
variations.description: Platforms that electrify chemical synthesis (replacing heat and stoichiometric redox reagents with electrons) or use high-throughput experimentation and AI to discover catalysts and greener electrochemical routes.

companies.name: Mattiq
companies.what: Combinatorial nanomaterials synthesis plus AI to discover catalysts (e.g., low/no-iridium for clean hydrogen) and electrified chemical processes.
companies.signal: ~$20M pre-Series A; Heraeus partnership (Jan 2025) to commercialize low-iridium catalysts; spun out of HydroGen/Chan Zuckerberg-linked efforts.

companies.name: Sunthetics
companies.what: AI (Bayesian) optimization platform for chemical R&D, including pulsed electro-organic synthesis that replaces heat-intensive reactions.
companies.signal: $4M seed (Nov 2024, L'ATTITUDE Ventures); 2025 ACS Green Chemistry Award with Merck; cut some R&D timelines from months to weeks.

companies.name: Chemify
companies.what: AI plus robotic "chemputer" platform that designs and automates synthesis routes for molecules and catalysts.
companies.signal: ~$43M Series A (2024); University of Glasgow (Cronin lab) spin-out; route/catalyst discovery as a service.

variations.white_space: Electro-organic synthesis at scale and AI catalyst discovery are nascent: few standalone companies exist because incumbents capture most value through internal R&D and economics hinge on cheap clean power and proven electrode durability. The opening is modular electrochemical reactors for high-value pharma/specialty intermediates and AI catalyst-discovery offered as a service to chemical majors.
